+## Review Findings (2026-11-01 07:33)
+
+> Scope: `review file` on each of the 12 files of the last implement pass, one for each call, 0 not reviewed: `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/{Evaluate,GenerationLoop,GenerateTokens,TokenIterators,MTPSpeculativeTokenIterator}.swift`, `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/{TranscriptConverter,MLXLanguageModelGeneration}.swift`, `Tests/MLXFoundationModelsTests/{ScriptedModelTestSupport,RequiredToolCallEnvelopeTests}.swift`, `Tests/MLXLMTests/{GenerationExecutionTests,MTPStatsCollectingTests,MTPGenerateLoopTaskContractTests}.swift`. A finding stands here when it sits on code that pass wrote or rewrote, the new `runTokenLoop` included. The `Evaluate.swift:164` items also cover `Evaluate.swift:101`.
+
+- [ ] `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/Evaluate.swift:164` `duplication/duplication` — The deprecated low-level `generate(input:context:iterator:didGenerate:)` repeats the `runSynchronousGenerationLoop` argument list from the sibling overload. Both pass `input.text.tokens.size`, `context.configuration`, `context.tokenizer`, and `iterator`, so a change to how the loop is fed must be made twice. Extract a private helper that takes `(input, context, iterator)` and returns `SynchronousGenerationLoopResult`, or the `runSynchronousGenerationLoop` call itself. Both overloads then parameterize only the visitor and the result mapping.
+- [ ] `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/Evaluate.swift:164` `reuse/reuse` — The `GenerateCompletionInfo`-returning deprecated `generate(input:context:iterator:didGenerate:)` repeats the `runSynchronousGenerationLoop` call of the `GenerateResult`-returning overload (lines 101-108). The same four arguments are passed in the same order, and only the per-token closure and the returned projection differ. A fix to the loop call has to be made in both places. Have the `GenerateCompletionInfo` overload call the `GenerateResult` overload's loop through a shared private helper that takes the `SynchronousGenerationLoopResult`, or extract the argument list into one private helper that both overloads call. Keep each overload's closure and projection at its own call site.
+- [ ] `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/GenerationLoop.swift:132` `swift/immutability` — `runSynchronousGenerationLoop` is an internal top-level function, visible to every file in the module with no namespace. Make it a `static func` on a namespace type, for example `enum SynchronousGenerationLoop { static func run(...) }`, or move it into an extension of the iterator protocol.
+- [ ] `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/GenerationLoop.swift:172` `hand-check` — The split made `GeneratedTokenCollector` internal, and with it `drafterContinuation(leftBy:)`, which was confined to its file while the protocol was private. Its three callers are all in GenerationLoop.swift, so the visibility is wider than the split needs. Declare it `fileprivate static func drafterContinuation(leftBy:)`.
+- [ ] `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/GenerationLoop.swift:326` `hand-check` — The doc comment of `runTokenLoop` says "Every generation path runs this one loop". `GuidedGenerationLoop.run` and `GuidedSpeculation` drive grammar-constrained generation through loops of their own and cannot reach this private function, so the statement is false. Name the paths the loop serves: the paths that go through `generateLoopTask` and `runSynchronousGenerationLoop`.
+- [ ] `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/GenerationLoop.swift:420` `completeness/invariant-propagation` — The stop-token predicate and the handler-delivery predicate disagree about the unknown token. `isStopToken` (line 50) treats `tokenizer.unknownTokenId` as a stop token, so line 411 ends the loop on it. The delivery check at line 420 requires `stopTokenIds.contains(token)`, which does not include `unknownTokenId`. A handler with `receivesStopTokens == true` therefore never receives the stop event when generation ends on the unknown token, although it does receive the other stop tokens. The same treatment is missing at this second consumer of the stop set. Make both predicates use one definition of 'stop'. Either route line 420 through `isStopToken(token, tokenizer:, stopTokenIds:)`, or state in the doc comment that unknown-token terminations are never delivered to `receivesStopTokens` handlers, and add a test that pins that behavior.
+- [ ] `Tests/MLXFoundationModelsTests/RequiredToolCallEnvelopeTests.swift:21` `completeness/inverse-operation-coverage` — The suite only exercises the rejection direction of `emitRequiredToolCallEvent`: non-JSON output and a nameless envelope both expect `false`. No test feeds a well-formed envelope with a name and expects `true`. An implementation that always returns `false` would pass both tests, so the suite does not prove the parser can accept the input it exists to accept. Add one positive test, for example `#expect(try await emits(#"{\"name\":\"f\",\"arguments\":{}}"#))`, so the accepting direction of the envelope parser is exercised alongside the two drop cases.
+- [ ] `Tests/MLXFoundationModelsTests/RequiredToolCallEnvelopeTests.swift:23` `swift/optionals` — A `guard ... else { return }` sits in a test. A `guard` that returns exits the test before its assertion runs, so a test that cannot reach its assertion reports as a pass instead of a failure. Remove the early return. Keep the `@available` annotation on the test function or suite so the test runs only where the API exists. If a runtime check is still needed, state the requirement as an assertion, for example `#expect(#available(iOS 27.0, macOS 27.0, visionOS 27.0, *))`, so an unexpected platform fails visibly.
+- [ ] `Tests/MLXFoundationModelsTests/RequiredToolCallEnvelopeTests.swift:29` `swift/optionals` — The same `guard ... else { return }` appears in a second test. It exits before the assertion on line 30, so a broken program passes silently. Remove the early return and rely on the `@available` annotation on the test function or suite, or assert the availability condition explicitly, as in the fix for line 23.
+
